Tumour-innervating nociceptor neurons promote immunosuppression

a, In oral melanoma and head and neck tumours, reactive oxygen species (ROS) produced within malignant cells lead to the phosphorylation of JUN, activating the transcription of nerve growth factor (NGF). NGF is then secreted and binds to its receptor tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TRKA) on tumour-innervating nociceptor neurons, promoting peri-tumoural neurogenesis, increased transcription of calcitonin-related polypeptide-α (CALCA; the gene encoding calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)) and secretion of CGRP. CGRP then binds to the receptor activity-modifying protein 1 (RAMP1)–calcitonin gene-related peptide type 1 receptor (CALCRL) receptor complex on malignant cells, promoting tumour growth and cytoprotective autophagy via the mTOR–Raptor pathway. Blocking the CGRP–RAMP1 axis using the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug rimegepant reverses these effects77. b, Melanoma cells secrete the neuron-activating molecule secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor (SLPI), which leads to the release of CGRP. CGRP, in turn, activates RAMP1 on CD8+ T cells, driving the exhaustion of effector T cells, as evidenced by the upregulation of immune checkpoint molecules such as PD1, lymphocyte-activation gene 3 (LAG3) and T cell immunoglobulin mucin receptor 3 (TIM3)64,71. c, In melanoma, sensory/sympathetic denervation (SSD) recruits both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, promoting the formation of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and enhancing antitumour immunity63. Intratumoural high endothelial venules are specialized blood vessels resembling those found in lymphoid organs, and have a crucial role in facilitating lymphocyte infiltration into the tumour microenvironment (TME). SSD promotes the generation of intratumoural high endothelial venules, thereby increasing the trafficking of inflammatory effector T cells to the tumour. Collectively, these events foster the emergence of structures similar to TLS in the TME, resulting in more durable antitumour immune responses. d, In breast cancer, substance P interacts with its receptor neurokinin 1 receptor (NK1R) to stimulate cancer cell proliferation and lymph node metastasis. Apoptotic NK1Rhigh cancer cells release single-stranded RNA, which activates Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) on other malignant cells and, in turn, induces a pro-metastatic gene profile leading to growth and metastasis, leading to decreased survival83. The NK1R inhibitor aprepitant can reverse these effects. Neuro-targeted therapies — including RAMP1 antagonists (for example, rimegepant or BIBN4096 (also known as olcegepant)), neuron silencing agents (for example, the quaternary (lidocaine-derived) local anaesthetic QX-314, botulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) and NK1R inhibitors (aprepitant)) — show promise in reducing cancer-induced neuro-immune interactions, curbing tumour growth and metastasis while improving survival outcomes (panels b and d).
